C004.subject: Text-only scaling paradigms
C004.object: human-level AGI on abstract reasoning tasks that require causal understanding of physical systems
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Text-only scaling paradigms human-level AGI on abstract reasoning tasks that require causal understanding of physical systems]

[PATH:empirical] Systematic comparison of LLMs (e.g., GPT-4, Gemini) vs. humans on the Physical Reasoning and Causal Understanding benchmark (e.g., PHYRE, CLEVRER, or the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) — Directly tests whether text-only models can match human performance on tasks requiring causal understanding of physical systems; failure would support the hypothesis, while success would refute it.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of the limitations of purely statistical language models for causal reasoning (e.g., Pearl's causal hierarchy and the 'no free lunch' theorems for learning causal structures from text) — Provides formal arguments that text-only scaling cannot acquire the necessary causal models without embodied interaction, strengthening the hypothesis if no counterexamples emerge.

[PATH:literature] Literature review of existing research on 'embodied' vs. 'disembodied' AI reasoning (e.g., studies comparing performance of text-only models vs. models with access to simulated physical environments) — Synthesizes empirical results from multiple studies to see if a consensus exists that text-only paradigms plateau on physical causality tasks, confirming or refuting the hypothesis.

C005.subject: Embodied interaction
C005.object: achieving human-level AGI on abstract reasoning tasks
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Embodied interaction achieving human-level AGI on abstract reasoning tasks]

[PATH:empirical] Comparative study of abstract reasoning performance between embodied AI agents (e.g., robotic manipulation in physical or high-fidelity simulated environments) and disembodied large language models on tasks like Raven's Progressive Matrices or ARC-AGI, controlling for training data and compute. — Directly tests whether physical interaction (e.g., manipulating objects to infer rules) yields superior generalization or causal understanding compared to purely symbolic/statistical reasoning, providing a clean contrast for the necessity claim.

[PATH:theoretical] Systematic literature review of cognitive science and developmental psychology studies on the role of sensorimotor experience in human abstract concept formation (e.g., Piaget's stages, embodied cognition theories like Lakoff & Johnson). — Establishes whether embodied interaction is a necessary precondition for human-level abstract reasoning, which would support the hypothesis if analogous constraints apply to AI, or refute it if symbolic reasoning alone suffices in humans.

[PATH:empirical] Ablation study on a hybrid neuro-symbolic AGI architecture that progressively removes or degrades embodied input channels (e.g., vision, tactile, proprioception) while measuring performance on abstract reasoning benchmarks, using a platform like Habitat or MuJoCo. — Provides causal evidence: if performance significantly degrades without embodiment, it confirms necessity; if not, it refutes the hypothesis under current paradigms.

C006.subject: Text-only scaling paradigms augmented with causal learning mechanisms
C006.object: human-level AGI that requires causal understanding of physical environments
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Text-only scaling paradigms augmented with causal learning mechanisms human-level AGI that requires causal understanding of physical environments]

[PATH:empirical] Controlled experiments comparing performance of text-only causal models (e.g., GPT-4 with causal fine-tuning) against embodied agents (e.g., in MuJoCo or Habitat) on physical reasoning tasks like object permanence, tool use, or intuitive physics benchmarks (e.g., PHYRE, CLEVRER) — Directly tests whether text-only scaling with added causal mechanisms can match or exceed the physical understanding of embodied systems, providing quantitative evidence for or against the hypothesis.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of the computational limits of text-only representations for grounding physical causality, e.g., using the 'symbol grounding problem' literature (Harnad, 1990) or recent work on the necessity of sensorimotor experience for learning causal structures (e.g., Lake et al., 2017; Bisk et al., 2020) — Establishes whether there are in-principle limitations to text-only models acquiring the kind of causal understanding required for physical environments, independent of current empirical results.

[PATH:literature] Systematic literature review of benchmarks and results from the 'Causal World' and 'EmbodiedQA' research programs, comparing text-only causal learning approaches (e.g., causal language models, Causal-BERT) to those using interactive or visual data — Synthesizes existing evidence on whether causal mechanisms added to text-only models close the gap with embodied models, identifying consistent patterns or counterexamples across studies.

C007.subject: Text-only scaling paradigms
C007.object: developing human-level AGI with causal understanding of physical environments
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Text-only scaling paradigms developing human-level AGI with causal understanding of physical environments]

[PATH:empirical] Controlled experiments comparing causal reasoning performance (e.g., physical object interaction tasks, counterfactual prediction) between large language models (text-only) and embodied agents trained with sensorimotor data. — Directly tests whether text-only models can develop causal understanding of physical environments equivalent to that of agents with embodied experience; if text-only models fail on tasks requiring physical intuition (e.g., predicting object stability or collision outcomes), the hypothesis is refuted.

[PATH:theoretical] Theoretical analysis of causal representation learning in transformer-based language models, e.g., examining whether attention patterns and latent representations capture compositional physical causality (e.g., force, mass, friction) from text alone, using interpretability tools like probing or causal tracing. — Provides mechanistic evidence for or against the sufficiency of text-only scaling: if models can be shown to extract and manipulate causal physical concepts purely from linguistic data, the hypothesis gains support; if not, it suggests inherent limitations.

[PATH:literature] Systematic literature review of recent benchmarks for physical causal reasoning (e.g., PIQA, PhysicalQA, CausalWorld) comparing performance of text-only LLMs vs. multimodal or embodied systems, with meta-analysis of failure patterns. — Aggregates existing empirical evidence across multiple studies to assess the trend: if text-only models consistently underperform on tasks requiring causal understanding of physical dynamics, this refutes the hypothesis; if performance gaps are closing with scale, it may be confirmed.
